claims.text: The as-solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy has a single-phase FCC matrix and a uniform microstructure.
Dynamic loading can induce an FCC-to-BCC martensitic transformation in FeNiCrMn.
The deformation-induced BCC phase occupies only a minor volume fraction.
The proposed FCC-to-BCC transformation is favored by low temperature.
The proposed FCC-to-BCC transformation is favored by high strain rate.
The deformation-induced transformation produces transformation-induced plasticity.
The BCC phase is harder than the FCC matrix.
Formation of the BCC phase increases strain hardening.
The increased strain hardening delays the onset of necking.
Delayed necking helps FeNiCrMn maintain its strength–ductility balance.
Under cryogenic, high-strain-rate loading, reproducible minor BCC diffraction peaks should appear.
The appearance of BCC phase should correlate with increased work-hardening rate relative to the baseline FCC state.
The hypothesis is intended to apply from approximately 77 K to 298 K and through quasi-static and split-Hopkinson-type high-strain-rate regimes.
Testing phase evolution with synchrotron X-ray diffraction, EBSD, and in-situ TEM can assess whether the proposed transformation occurs.
Failure to detect a BCC transformation under the specified dynamic conditions would falsify the hypothesis.
The detailed falsification rule requires both no detectable BCC phase and no significant increase in work hardening relative to the baseline.
Any transformation below the instruments' detection limits cannot be excluded by the proposed measurements.

contradictions.description: The predicted-outcome field says that failure to observe the phase transformation is sufficient to falsify the hypothesis, whereas the detailed rule requires both absence of detectable BCC and absence of a significant work-hardening increase. Thus, a test showing no BCC but increased work hardening has inconsistent falsification status.
